Cc: procurement@globex.com
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Performance projection & SLA synthesis questionnaire

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks for the introductory call yesterday. Globex is consolidating vendors for our conversational search platform and your platform is on the shortlist. Procurement asked me to gather a short, focused questionnaire that will let our engineering and infra teams validate whether Redwood can meet our SLA and throughput targets before the POC.

High-level asks:
- Concrete guidance on test methodology for latency (P50/P90/P99) and throughput (sustained QPS) across mixed prompt sizes.
- Recommended experiment matrix (concurrency ramps, burst tests, soak).
- Clear description of what is measured vs what we’ll need to measure on our side (tokens vs. requests, warm vs. cold cache).
- Any tooling you recommend or provide for replaying production traffic and synthetic load.
- Expected lead time and attachments needed if we ask Redwood to run a partner-managed benchmark in your infra.

I attached the RFP appendix with our target SLAs (attached as Globex_RFP_Attachments.zip). Can you confirm we’ll get a benchmarking plan this week? Our timeline is tight — procurement decision by Oct 1.

Appreciate a short, actionable reply and a proposed call slot if helpful.

Thanks,
Aria Singh
Senior Sourcing Manager — Globex Corporation

Aria — thanks for the clear asks and the RFP appendix. Attaching a concise benchmarking matrix (redwood_performance_matrix.xlsx) and a runnable checklist your infra team can follow. Below is a succinct plan so your engineers can triage immediately.

Summary (short):
- We can document expected P50/P90/P99 under your target prompt distributions and provide a partner-managed run in our Dedicated infra within 5 business days of signed NDA/test agreement.
- Run types we recommend: baseline (single client, cold start), steady-state (sustained QPS with warm KV cache), burst (sudden concurrency spikes), and soak (48h stability).

Recommended experiment matrix (high level):
1) Workload characterization
   - Provide 1k–5k representative requests (CSV) with actual token counts and sequence-length distribution. If unavailable, provide percentiles of sequence length (p10/p25/p50/p75/p90/p99).
2) Baseline latency profile (single client)
   - Run 1k sequential requests (no batching), measure tokenized latency, model compute time, and end-to-end RT (client to response). Sample stats: mean, std, P50/P90/P99.
3) Concurrency sweep
   - Sweep concurrent connections: 1, 5, 10, 25, 50, 100, 200. For each step, run 5 minutes steady-state at target QPS. Track latency percentiles and GPU utilization.
4) Batching & token throughput
   - If you plan to batch on client side, run identical tests with batch sizes 1, 2, 4, 8. Report tokens/sec and tokens/GPU-second.
5) Burst and tail behavior
   - Repeated microbursts (e.g., 10s at 5x baseline QPS) to surface queueing and scheduler fallbacks.
6) Soak and degradation modes
   - 48-hour soak at expected production QPS to exercise memory growth, KV cache hit-rate dynamics, and any slow memory leaks.

Test harness & tooling we use / recommend:
- Synthetic driver: our internal fork of Locust with token-aware payloads (we can share the runner).
- Production replay: we accept replay logs (redacted) in newline-delimited JSON; we will replay honoring original inter-arrival times if requested.
- Telemetry: we’ll stream a metrics dashboard (Prometheus + Grafana) with per-route latency, GPU util, NVLink stats, and per-token cost estimates.

What Redwood measures vs what we expect from Globex:
- Redwood will provide: per-request latency breakdown (client->proxy, model compute, kv-cache hit/miss), per-GPU utilization, memory footprint, and tokens/s. We will also surface model kernel selection and quantization profile used.
- Globex should provide: representative traces or distribution summaries, target SLOs, and any variance constraints (e.g., 99th percentile latency must be < 300ms for short prompts).

Acceptance & reporting:
- After each run we’ll produce a short report with charts and a recommendations section: tuning batch sizes, quantization tradeoffs, autoscaling curve, and fallback policy suggestions.

Logistics and attachments needed for a partner-managed run:
- NDA/test agreement (we can provide a short draft)
- Representative request samples or distribution summary
- Target model(s) (open model name and size) and sequence length expectations

Timeline estimate (partner-managed run):
- Day 0: NDA + sample data received
- Day 1: environment & harness prep (we'll share the runner)
- Day 2: baseline & concurrency sweep
- Day 3: soak starts (24–48h)
- Day 5: final report delivered (with attachments)

Next steps:
- I can run a short scoping call with your infra engineers — propose Wed 15 Sep 10:00–11:00 PT or Thu 16 Sep 14:00–15:00 PT. Which works?

Notes and constraints:
- Warm vs cold cache: our platform exposes KV cache hit-rate. Cold-start latency for very long context windows (>4096 tokens) can be significantly higher; we’ll flag that in the report.
- Model variants: when capacity constrained we may suggest a quantized variant; we’ll provide head-to-head latency/quality tradeoffs.

Attached: redwood_performance_matrix.xlsx (matrix + run checklist).

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Enterprise Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Performance projection & SLA synthesis questionnaire

Aria — quick note from infra: two pragmatic items to watch during your runs.

1) Canary & fallback: run a limited canary (1–2% traffic) against Dedicated capacity first. If P99 drift > 2x baseline, our routing will failover to a lower-latency variant or higher-capacity pool; we’ll capture failover latency but it will count as a separate telemetry bucket.
2) Cost signal: for very high token volumes, GPU-hours and egress dominate. In the report we’ll include tokens/GPU-hour and tokens/$ to help procurement compare unit economics.

Attached: redwood_benchmark_summary.pdf (summary of prior partner-managed runs showing tokens/sec and tail latency under similar workloads).

Ben Carter
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

- Can we take the Wed 15 Sep slot? It looks like it conflicts for us — propose Fri 17 Sep 09:00–09:45 PT or Mon 20 Sep 14:00–14:45 PT.

Procurement note: we are evaluating unit economics across three vendors; please include tokens/GPU-hour and a simple cost projection for a representative monthly volume of 500M tokens.

Thanks again — look forward to the scoping call.

Best,
Aria Singh
Senior Sourcing Manager — Globex Corporation
